explanations: luna: The section’s secondary dictionary form الخلاق means a share; this verse says the buyer has no “خلاق” in the Hereafter, using that same share sense. | terra: مَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ uses the section's named derivative خلاق in its exact sense "allotted share," here a share forfeited in the hereafter.
terra: The person who asks only for this world has وَمَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَٰقٍ, showing خلاق as a measured portion rather than creation.

luna: The section names ق د ر as measure and boundary; “على الموسع قدره وعلى المقتر قدره” sets a financial obligation according to each person’s means, a specific application of measured capacity. | terra: عَلَى ٱلْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُۥ وَعَلَى ٱلْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُۥ makes a gift proportionate to each person's capacity, a practical instance of measured portion.

luna: The section describes the eyes, tongue, and lips as measured parts of a created human; this says God forms people in the wombs as He wills, a specific image of bodily shaping. | terra: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ locates deliberate bodily formation in the womb and attributes it to the one irresistible God.

luna: The section labels الخلاق as an allotted share; “لا خلاق لهم في الآخرة” uses the same word for those with no share in the Hereafter. | terra: Those who trade God's covenant and their oaths لَا خَلَٰقَ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ, bringing oath and the derivative meaning "share" into one judgment.

luna: The section’s dictionary gloss for الخلاق is a person’s نصيب, or share; this verse explicitly assigns “نصيب” to men and women, making an individual portion concrete. | terra: Men and women each have نَصِيبًا مَّفْرُوضًا from an estate; this legally fixed share makes concrete the section's definition of a portion measured for each person.

luna: The section’s ق س م root denotes division into shares; this verse names “القسمة” of an estate and directs that nearby relatives, orphans, and the poor receive provision from it. | terra: When dependants, orphans, and the poor attend ٱلْقِسْمَةَ, they too are to be provided, joining division of property to responsibility for one's share.
luna: The section says each person’s share is measured; this verse assigns specified fractions to heirs and calls them an obligation from God, a legal example of apportioned shares.
luna: The section’s share image is an allotment measured for each person; this verse gives spouses and siblings fixed fractions, showing that portions can be precisely set.
luna: After the fixed portions in 4:11–12, this verse calls them “حدود الله”; it makes the section’s measure-as-limit concrete in the laws of allotted shares.
terra: Men and women each have نَصِيبٌۭ مِّمَّا ٱكْتَسَبُوا۟, while envy is redirected toward asking God's bounty; shares are received within divine apportionment.
terra: وَلِكُلٍّ جَعَلْنَا ... فَـَٔاتُوهُمْ نَصِيبَهُمْ brings "for each," جعل, and an owed share together under God's witness.
terra: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ حَسِيبًا extends حساب from human counting to the One who takes account of every thing.
luna: The section’s 90:7 challenges the thought that no one saw the man; these people hide from other people but “ولا يستخفون من الله,” distinguishing human secrecy from divine sight.
terra: إِنَّمَا ٱللَّهُ إِلَٰهٌ وَٰحِدٌ ... أَن يَكُونَ لَهُۥ وَلَدٌ explicitly joins divine oneness to transcendence beyond having a child.
luna: The section’s share image is a measured portion for each person; this final inheritance ruling specifies fractions for siblings and completes another instance of divided shares.
terra: مِن قَبْلِ أَن تَقْدِرُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمْ uses the same قدر على construction for gaining power over persons, confirming the section's lexical sense of mastery in a human legal setting.
terra: If God touches a person with harm no one removes it but Him, and وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ states the power excluded by the man's boast.
terra: وَمَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦ identifies denial of revelation as failure to measure God truly, another form of setting a false limit on Him.

luna: The section labels ح س ب as counting or estimating; here the sun and moon are made “حسبانا,” so celestial order itself supplies a reckoning against human guesswork. | terra: God جَعَلَ night for rest and the sun and moon حُسْبَانًا, then calls their courses تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ; making, calculation, and measure meet.
terra: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلنُّجُومَ لِتَهْتَدُوا۟ continues 6:96 from measured heavenly signs to guidance, paralleling "measured, then guided."
terra: How could God have a child without a consort when وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ? The ayah explicitly distinguishes the Creator of every thing from generated parenthood.
terra: Humans جَعَلُوا۟ ... نَصِيبًا for God and partners بِزَعْمِهِمْ; their invented partition opposes the Creator's measured share and rests on mere claim.
luna: The section’s share image is an allotted portion of provision; this orders people to give its due on harvest, making a claim on measured produce explicit.
luna: The section’s image of measure and assigned limits extends to judgment here: “والوزن يومئذ الحق” makes weighing the standard on that Day.
luna: Following 7:8’s true weighing, this verse says those whose scales are heavy succeed and those whose scales are light lose themselves; it gives the outcome of measured deeds.
terra: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَٰكُمْ explicitly follows creation with bodily shaping, matching the section's sense of material cut to form.
luna: The section says shares are assigned by measure; this divides captured goods by specifying a fifth for God, the Messenger, and named recipients.
terra: وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ ... سَبَقُوٓا۟ إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ forbids the thought that wrongdoers have outrun the One who can seize them.
terra: أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تُتْرَكُوا۟ rejects the supposition that people are simply left before their loyalties become known to God.
terra: فَٱسْتَمْتَعُوا۟ بِخَلَٰقِهِمْ ... بِخَلَٰقِكُمْ uses خلاق twice for each people's allotted worldly portion and warns against mistaking that portion for immunity.

luna: The section connects ق د ر with measured limits and ح س ب with counting; the moon is set in phases so people know years and reckoning, linking measured creation to human counting. | terra: The moon is given measured stations so people know عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلْحِسَابَ, while مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ذَٰلِكَ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ joins creation to true counting.
terra: The claim that God took a child is answered هُوَ ٱلْغَنِىُّ and by His ownership of all things, locating true self-sufficiency with the Creator.

luna: The section’s dictionary sense of ق د ر is a thing’s reached extent and limit; “وكل شيء عنده بمقدار” places every matter within a measure held by God. | terra: After measuring what wombs lose and gain, the ayah says وَكُلُّ شَىْءٍ عِندَهُۥ بِمِقْدَارٍ; birth and every thing have a known extent with God.
terra: When God intends harm فَلَا مَرَدَّ لَهُۥ and there is no protector besides Him, setting a firm boundary against the thought of being unreachable.
terra: Rain sends valleys flowing بِقَدَرِهَا, so each channel receives according to its capacity; this concretizes measure as a thing's extent and limit.

luna: The section’s ق د ر branch includes constricted provision; this contrasts God’s expansion of provision with “ويقدر,” showing that the root’s measure sense also governs livelihood. | terra: ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقْدِرُ places expansion and restriction with God, while its recipients rejoice wrongly in the nearer life.
terra: وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا contrasts human inability to enumerate divine gifts with the boastful man's count of wealth.
terra: وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَٰفِلًا عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ directly rejects the thought that oppressive deeds have escaped the divine witness.
terra: أَوَلَمْ تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَقْسَمْتُم ... مَا لَكُم مِّن زَوَالٍ recalls an oath that they would never pass away, joining قسم to denial of the appointed limit.
terra: The earth yields مِن كُلِّ شَىْءٍ مَّوْزُونٍ, a nonlexical parallel in which created growth comes in balanced measure.

luna: The section connects ق د ر to measured provision and each person’s allotment; this says what is sent down comes “بقدر معلوم,” making provision’s measure explicit. | terra: Divine stores descend only بِقَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ, presenting provision itself as a known measured portion.
terra: لِكُلِّ بَابٍ مِّنْهُمْ جُزْءٌ مَّقْسُومٌ gives each gate an assigned portion, concretely combining "for each," part, and division.
terra: وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَا repeats the boundary on human counting in a passage about God's manifold provisions.
terra: They أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ that God will not raise the dead; their oath embodies a false human estimate of divine power that God's promise reverses.
terra: People يَجْعَلُونَ ... نَصِيبًا from God's provision for what they do not know, another invented share that will be questioned.
terra: God has preferred some over others in provision, while those favored resist making dependants equal partners in it; the ayah probes ownership of an allotted share.
terra: The owned servant لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ is contrasted with one given good provision who spends from it, placing ability, ownership, allotted rizq, and expenditure in one parable.

luna: The section describes the eyes as parts made for a human; this says people emerge from their mothers’ wombs knowing nothing and are given hearing, sight, and hearts. | terra: God brings humans from wombs unknowing and جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ, making faculties gifts fitted to the newborn.
luna: The section’s dictionary image measures leather before cutting it into a waterskin; this verse describes cattle hides made into portable dwellings, showing hide shaped for a practical use.
luna: The section names ح س ب as counting; this says the alternation of night and day lets people know the number of years and reckoning, an ordered count rather than mere supposition.
terra: كَفَىٰ بِنَفْسِكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكَ حَسِيبًا turns the final record into an account the person himself cannot deny.
terra: ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ فَضَّلْنَا بَعْضَهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ asks the reader to observe differentiated shares and says the hereafter has still greater ranks.

luna: The section identifies the ق د ر root’s provision sense as narrowing what is given; this says God expands provision for some and “يقدر” for others. | terra: God يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ and is خَبِيرًۢا بَصِيرًا, joining measured provision to the seeing knowledge denied by the boastful man.
terra: The ayah joins خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ, power to create humans again, and a جَعَلَ fixed term, uniting craft, ability, and limit.
terra: God shares His judgment with وَلَا يُشْرِكُ فِى حُكْمِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا; the negative أَحَد belongs properly to exclusive divine rule.
terra: أَنَا۠ أَكْثَرُ مِنكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا voices the wealthy man's count of assets and supporters as a claim to superior power.
terra: مَآ أَظُنُّ أَن تَبِيدَ هَٰذِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا turns counted wealth into a false supposition that the garden has no limit.
terra: His companion answers with the One who خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا, opposing the boast with created, proportioned origin.
terra: The garden owner is taught to say مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ, replacing confidence in his estate with the admission that power belongs to God.
terra: The fruit is encompassed and its owner wrings his hands over what he spent, an enacted reversal of his estimate that the garden could not perish.
terra: After the garden's loss he has no group to help him besides God وَمَا كَانَ مُنتَصِرًا, a concrete end to the belief that one's holdings secure power.
terra: The record leaves neither small nor great إِلَّآ أَحْصَىٰهَا; exact divine counting corrects the man's count of wealth and his belief that no one saw.
terra: قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُم بِٱلْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَٰلًا introduces 18:104's people whose self-measure of their work is opposite to its real outcome.

luna: The section distinguishes the ح س ب root’s counting sense from a person’s mistaken supposition; these people “يحسبون أنهم يحسنون صنعا” while their worldly effort is lost, a concrete false self-assessment. | terra: وَهُمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ صُنْعًا identifies the greatest losers by a mistaken assessment of their own making.
terra: مَا كَانَ لِلَّهِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ مِن وَلَدٍ separates the One from offspring, while His decree "Be" identifies creation rather than begetting as His act.
terra: إِنَّمَا نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ عَدًّا says God is counting out the wrongdoers' remaining time, a precise reversal of their impatience and imagined freedom.
terra: وَمَا يَنۢبَغِى لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدًا sets a firm boundary between the Creator and generated offspring.
terra: Every being in heaven and earth comes to the Merciful only as a servant, supplying the creature–Creator relation that replaces divine parenthood.
terra: لَّقَدْ أَحْصَىٰهُمْ وَعَدَّهُمْ عَدًّا says every servant has been encompassed and counted exactly, leaving no anonymous "no one" outside the One's knowledge.
terra: وَكُلُّهُمْ ءَاتِيهِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فَرْدًا gives the consequence of 19:94: each measured person comes to God alone.

luna: Moses describes the Lord as the one who gave each thing its created form (“أعطى كل شيء خلقه”) and then guided it; this joins the section’s shaped creation to its later guidance. | terra: Moses identifies the Lord as the One who أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ: each thing receives its fitted creation and then its way.

luna: The section’s man presumes no one can set a limit on him; this places just scales on the Day of Resurrection and says no soul is wronged, even by a mustard-seed weight. | terra: The just balances omit nothing, even a mustard seed, and وَكَفَىٰ بِنَا حَٰسِبِينَ identifies God as the sufficient reckoner.

luna: The section’s root ق د ر moves between power and measure; Jonah’s “ظن أن لن نقدر عليه” repeats the claim’s exact construction, then his call in darkness shows where that presumption turns. | terra: Jonah's فَظَنَّ أَن لَّن نَّقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ reproduces the section's ظن/لن/نقدر/عليه pattern; his call from the darkness shows mistaken reckoning yielding to return.
terra: فَٱسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُۥ وَنَجَّيْنَٰهُ مِنَ ٱلْغَمِّ supplies the result of Jonah's call in 21:87: return to God, rather than presumed escape from His measure, brings rescue.
terra: The full sequence from dust and drop through womb, birth, maturity, and death makes bodily creation a measured progression to an appointed term and evidence for resurrection.
terra: وَمَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦ ... إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ directly opposes faulty human estimation to divine strength.
terra: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَانَ مِن سُلَٰلَةٍ مِّن طِينٍ begins a workshop-like account of the human's material formation.
terra: ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَٰهُ نُطْفَةً فِى قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ joins جعل to the fitted placement of the created human in the womb.
terra: Successive bodily forms culminate in خَلْقًا ءَاخَرَ and أَحْسَنُ ٱلْخَٰلِقِينَ, making creation an ordered transformation of material.
terra: Water descends بِقَدَرٍ while God is عَلَىٰ ذَهَابٍۭ بِهِۦ لَقَٰدِرُونَ, setting measured provision and sovereign ability side by side in one scene.
terra: أَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّمَا نُمِدُّهُم بِهِۦ مِن مَّالٍ وَبَنِينَ asks whether recipients suppose wealth and sons have the meaning they assign to them.
terra: نُسَارِعُ لَهُمْ فِى ٱلْخَيْرَٰتِ rejects that supposition: an enlarged share is not itself a verdict of favor.
terra: وَلَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا gives each soul a bounded capacity, while the truthful record prevents that measure from becoming arbitrary.
terra: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ is a direct counterpart to eyes, tongue, and lips as created parts.
terra: God has taken no child and has no co-god; otherwise each deity would take بِمَا خَلَقَ and seek to overpower the other, joining creation to exclusive power.
luna: The section’s ح س ب root includes supposing and its خ ل ق image is purposeful measured creation; this asks whether people thought they were created in vain and would not return to God.
terra: وَتَحْسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ contrasts human assessment with God's, showing that حسب can badly mismeasure a deed.
terra: The thirsty person يَحْسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمْـَٔانُ مَآءً follows a false visual estimate to its endpoint, where he finds God and receives his full حساب.
terra: لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ ... مُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ directly couples false supposition with the imagined ability to frustrate God's power.

luna: The section’s root خ ل ق means measured making and its ق د ر root names measure; “خلق كل شيء فقدره تقديرا” states both actions together. | terra: The Creator who "created everything" then فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا states outright the section's sequence from crafting to exact measure.
terra: تَقَاسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ turns the oath-root into a collectively measured plan to attack Ṣāliḥ's household and then control the account of what happened.
terra: وَمَكَرُوا۟ مَكْرًا وَمَكَرْنَا مَكْرًا وَهُمْ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ sets the conspirators' calculation against a divine plan they do not perceive.
terra: Their destruction is the visible outcome of 27:49-50, showing how completely their sworn estimate of power failed.
terra: صُنْعَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ names God's making as work perfected in every thing, a nonlexical parallel to straight, exact measure.
terra: Qarun says إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُۥ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عِندِى, claiming his huge share as the product of his own calculation despite stronger predecessors destroyed by God.
terra: Qarun's display makes people who desire the nearer life wish for مِثْلَ مَآ أُوتِىَ قَٰرُونُ, showing how spectators misread another's allotted share.
terra: Those given knowledge call God's reward better, supplying the correct counter-measure to the worldly wish in 28:79 before Qarun's fall.
terra: When the earth swallows Qarun, no faction can help him and he cannot help himself, the enacted reversal of wealth-based invulnerability before 28:82 names provision's true allocator.

luna: The section connects ق د ر with measured provision; after Qarun’s wealth is swallowed, observers say Allah “يبسط الرزق ... ويقدر,” reading wealth as allotted rather than self-secured. | terra: After Qarun's fall, observers learn that God يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ and that their earlier wish for his allotment misread its meaning.

luna: The section distinguishes the ح س ب root’s counting from supposition and describes a person who presumes no one can constrain him; this asks whether people think they will be left untested. | terra: أَحَسِبَ ٱلنَّاسُ أَن يُتْرَكُوٓا۟ asks whether people suppose they will be left merely on their claim of faith, paralleling the thought of being left untested and unbounded.
luna: Following 29:2’s question about expecting no trial, this verse says earlier peoples were tested; it supplies the actual limit that the preceding presumption denies.
terra: أَمْ حَسِبَ ... أَن يَسْبِقُونَا asks whether evildoers calculate that they can get ahead of God, a precise parallel to imagined unreachability.
terra: وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ denies every location from which humans might frustrate God.

luna: The section says every person’s share is measured and links ق د ر to provision; this states that God expands livelihood or “يقدر له” for His servants. | terra: ٱللَّهُ يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ makes differing livelihood an act of the One who knows every thing.

luna: The section’s ق د ر root includes power and measure; this asks whether people see that God expands provision and “يقدر,” grounding human limits in divine allocation. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ asks people to see that God expands provision and يَقْدِرُ, answering both false interpretation and imagined lack of witness.
terra: God خَلَقَ humans from weakness, جَعَلَ strength and later weakness, and closes وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْقَدِيرُ; a whole life is shaped within His power.
terra: At the Hour criminals يُقْسِمُ ... مَا لَبِثُوا۟ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ; their oath embodies a false measurement of elapsed time even at judgment.
terra: مَّا خَلْقُكُمْ وَلَا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ وَٰحِدَةٍ makes the creation and resurrection of all humanity one act to the God who hears and sees.

luna: The section’s root خ ل ق describes measured making; this neighboring description says God perfected what He created and began human creation from clay, preparing the formed human of 32:8–9. | terra: ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْسَنَ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ describes created things as well-made work, supporting the artisan sense of خلق developed in the section.
luna: The section includes the parent and child in its whole-surah context and treats the human as created form; this verse places human offspring in a sequence beginning from an extract of fluid.

luna: The section says “ألم نجعل” belongs to the same work as creation and names eyes as made parts; this verse uses جعل for hearing, sight, and hearts after fashioning the human. | terra: ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُ ... وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ parallels the section's measured organs with proportioning followed by جعل.
terra: وَكَانَ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرًا مَّقْدُورًا expresses divine command as an appointed measure carried to its destined end.
terra: Messengers لَا يَخْشَوْنَ أَحَدًا إِلَّا ٱللَّهَ and God is sufficient حَسِيبًا, bringing "no one but God" together with the true reckoner.
terra: وَقَدِّرْ فِى ٱلسَّرْدِ commands David to measure the links while making armor, a literal artisan use of ق د ر like laying out leather before cutting.
terra: وَقَالُوا۟ نَحْنُ أَكْثَرُ أَمْوَٰلًا وَأَوْلَٰدًا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ voices the wealth-and-power inference that measured provision in 34:36 corrects.

luna: The section links measured power and provision through ق د ر; this says God expands livelihood and “يقدر,” while most people do not know the source of that measure. | terra: قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّى يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ answers the wealthy speakers of 34:35: abundance is allocation, not proof against punishment.
terra: وَمَآ أَمْوَٰلُكُمْ وَلَآ أَوْلَٰدُكُم بِٱلَّتِى تُقَرِّبُكُمْ rejects wealth and children as measures of nearness, completing the correction of 34:35-36.

luna: The section’s root ق د ر includes narrowing provision; this says God expands it or “يقدر له,” then promises replacement for what people spend. | terra: God يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ لَهُ and replaces what is spent, tying measured share to the man's boast about expenditure.
terra: Creation from dust and a drop, conception and birth by God's knowledge, and every extended or shortened life written down present generation and lifespan as measured together.
terra: They أَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ that a warner would make them better guided, but his arrival increases aversion; oath and claimed guidance expose a false self-measure.
terra: وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُعْجِزَهُۥ مِن شَىْءٍ denies that anything can defeat God's reach and grounds it in His knowledge and power.
terra: وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ فِىٓ إِمَامٍ مُّبِينٍ sets every act and trace within a complete divine count.

luna: The section’s root ق د ر joins measure and limit; the sun’s course is called “تقدير العزيز العليم,” a particular created order governed by measure. | terra: The sun's course is تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ, a visible created motion governed by the powerful Knower's determination.
terra: وَٱلْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَٰهُ مَنَازِلَ continues 36:38 with measured lunar stages, making determination a sequence of bounded stations.

luna: The section’s ق د ر root names power as well as measure; this asks whether the Creator of the heavens and earth is able to recreate people, turning the claim of limited power against itself. | terra: The One who created the heavens and earth is asked أَوَلَيْسَ ... بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم; creation establishes power to recreate.
terra: أَتَعْبُدُونَ مَا تَنْحِتُونَ introduces literal human carving, a concrete craft against which the Creator's work is distinguished.
terra: وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ answers the carving scene by placing both the artisans and their work under God's creation.
terra: وَمَا مِنَّآ إِلَّا لَهُۥ مَقَامٌ مَّعْلُومٌ gives every angel a known station, an indirect instance of a portion or limit assigned to each.
terra: The denial that God takes a child ends هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْوَٰحِدُ ٱلْقَهَّارُ, connecting the One beyond generation with irresistible power.
terra: خَلَقَكُم ... ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا and خَلْقًا مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ in three womb-darknesses join creation, making, generation, and divine kingship.
terra: وَبَدَا لَهُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُوا۟ يَحْتَسِبُونَ says divine judgment discloses what their reckoning never included.

luna: The section joins qadr with assigned provision; this asks whether people know that God expands provision and “يقدر,” a repeated statement of divinely measured livelihood. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوٓا۟ asks whether they know that God expands provision and يَقْدِرُ; the alternation is a sign, not their private verdict.
terra: وَمَا قَدَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِۦ names the human failure to estimate God, then the earth in His grasp displays the power their measure missed.
luna: The section names eyes as created parts and asks whether anyone saw the person; this says God knows furtive glances and what hearts conceal, joining sight to hidden acts.
terra: God صَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ and provided good things, joining fitted bodily form to provision.
terra: The human passes by God's creating through dust, drop, clot, birth, maturity, old age, and an appointed term, a direct anatomy of measure as an endpoint.
terra: وَقَدَّرَ فِيهَآ أَقْوَٰتَهَا apportions the earth's sustenance, a direct cosmic instance of the section's measured share.
luna: The section treats eyes as measured parts and asks whether anyone saw the man; this verse names hearing, sight, and skin as witnesses to deeds, giving those created parts an answering role.

luna: The section’s dictionary image measures hide before cutting it, while this verse has skins speak and says Allah created people the first time; it joins formed body, skin, and speech in one scene.

luna: The section’s 90:7 question imagines no one saw the man; here people had thought their hearing, eyes, and skins would not testify, but the verse says they wrongly thought Allah did not know their deeds.

luna: The section describes ق د ر as measure and limit; this verse says God expands provision or “يقدر” and closes by calling Him knowing of all things. | terra: The One who owns the keys of heaven and earth يَبْسُطُ ٱلرِّزْقَ ... وَيَقْدِرُ, grounding allotment in encompassing knowledge and ownership.
terra: The seeker of the world receives some of it but has no نَصِيبٍ in the hereafter, a non-خلاق formulation of the section's measured share and its horizon.

luna: The section links measure to each person’s provision; this says provision is sent down “بقدر ما يشاء,” making its measured distribution a divine act. | terra: God withholds unlimited provision lest people transgress and يُنَزِّلُ بِقَدَرٍ, making measure purposeful rather than humiliating.
terra: وَمَآ أَنتُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ and the absence of any protector or helper overturn the man's confidence that none can master him.
terra: God owns the dominion, يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ, and bestows daughters or sons as He wills; offspring are apportioned gifts, not human possession.
terra: God combines sons and daughters or يَجْعَلُ مَن يَشَآءُ عَقِيمًا and closes عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ, joining reproductive share, جعل, knowledge, and power.
terra: Water is sent from the sky بِقَدَرٍ and revives dead land, another concrete provision whose amount and effect are measured.

luna: The section’s ق س م dictionary note defines dividing into shares; “نحن قسمنا بينهم معيشتهم” applies that division to people’s livelihoods, joining allotment to provision. | terra: أَهُمْ يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ is answered by نَحْنُ قَسَمْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمْ, distinguishing human claims to divide from God's apportionment of livelihood.
terra: أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لَا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ asks whether hidden plotters suppose they go unheard, then says the messengers beside them write it down.
terra: أَمْ حَسِبَ ... أَن نَّجْعَلَهُمْ كَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ exposes a human calculation that wrongly assigns equal outcomes, placing حسب against God's just جعل.
terra: جَعَلْنَا لَهُمْ سَمْعًا وَأَبْصَٰرًا وَأَفْـِٔدَةً names the fitted faculties, then shows they avail nothing when God's signs are denied.
terra: The people are asked whether the Creator of the heavens and earth is بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يُحْـِۧىَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ, exposing their false boundary on divine power.
terra: أَمْ حَسِبَ ... أَن لَّن يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَٰنَهُمْ makes the false "hasiba an lan" concern what people think God will never expose.
luna: The section’s man assumes he is beyond another’s power or sight; this says the Creator knows what the self whispers, extending the limit from visible acts to private thought.

luna: The section’s ق س م root includes dividing and assigning portions; “فالمقسمات أمرا” names those who apportion affairs, extending that image to the distribution of commands. | terra: فَٱلْمُقَسِّمَٰتِ أَمْرًا evokes agents distributing the commanded affair, a likely instance of قسم as apportionment behind the section's oath-word.
terra: أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُونَ confronts humans with the impossible alternatives of being unmade or being their own makers.
terra: أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ extends 52:35 from self-creation to cosmic power and locates the error in their lack of certainty.

luna: The section labels خ ل ق’s source sense as straight measure and ق س م as dividing shares; this calls the self-serving assignment “قسمة ضيزى,” a crooked division, reversing that straight measure. | terra: تِلْكَ إِذًا قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ condemns the idolaters' division as unjust, a boundary between human partition and right apportionment.
terra: وَأَنَّهُۥ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ attributes the two sexes in the begetting scene to one Creator.
terra: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ gives 53:45 its generative material, keeping created sex and human procreation distinct.
terra: وَأَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلنَّشْأَةَ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰ carries the Creator's ownership of first formation into the second creation.
terra: Floodwaters meet عَلَىٰٓ أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ, giving ق د ر the sense of an event already carried to its appointed outcome.
terra: أَنَّ ٱلْمَآءَ قِسْمَةٌۢ بَيْنَهُمْ makes water an apportioned share between the people and the she-camel, a direct scene of قسم as division.

luna: The section treats creation as proportioned measure; “إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر” states that all created things are made according to measure. | terra: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَاهُ بِقَدَرٍ joins خ ل ق and ق د ر in one claim: every created thing already bears a measure.
luna: The section’s “خلقنا الإنسان” image is measured human creation; this verse likewise says the Merciful created the human, introducing the speech faculty in 55:4.
luna: The section names a tongue and lips among the human’s measured parts, and its man speaks his claim; “علمه البيان” connects those organs to articulate expression.

luna: The section contrasts human supposition with measured order and names the root ح س ب; “الشمس والقمر بحسبان” makes the sun and moon move by a reckoning. | terra: ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ presents حساب as exact ordered calculation rather than the man's unfounded guess.
terra: God raises heaven وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ, making balance part of the created order rather than a human invention.
terra: أَلَّا تَطْغَوْا۟ فِى ٱلْمِيزَانِ turns the given measure into a boundary humans must not overrun.
terra: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ commands humans to make their own measuring straight and not diminish the balance.
terra: نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ فَلَوْلَا تُصَدِّقُونَ makes "We created you" the answer to human denial, the stance underlying the section's measured human.
terra: ءَأَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُۥٓ أَمْ نَحْنُ ٱلْخَالِقُونَ excludes human ownership of his own formation and assigns the craft to God.
terra: نَحْنُ قَدَّرْنَا بَيْنَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتَ makes death itself an allotment "among you," joining measurement, division, and the limit no human escapes.
terra: عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّبَدِّلَ أَمْثَٰلَكُمْ completes 56:60 by naming the bodily replacement God's allotment cannot be prevented from accomplishing.
terra: أَحْصَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ contrasts God's complete count of deeds with human forgetting, and closes by calling God witness over everything.
terra: They swear to God as they swore to people وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍ; oath and supposition combine in an empty claim to standing.
terra: They ظَنُّوٓا۟ their fortresses would protect them from God, but He came مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا۟; human security fails exactly outside its reckoning.
terra: خَلَقَ ... بِٱلْحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ treats the human form as part of purposeful creation, not self-owned material.

luna: The section’s root ق د ر names measured bounds; “قد جعل الله لكل شيء قدرا” states that God has set a measure for everything. | terra: قَدْ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدْرًا combines جعل with a divinely set measure for every thing, and says that unexpected provision also lies within that measure.

luna: The section labels the ق د ر branch “ومن قدر عليه رزقه” as narrowed provision; this repeats that wording and commands spending from what was given within that limit. | terra: وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ gives the section's exact narrowed-provision construction and commands spending from what God gave within that limit.
terra: Creation of the seven heavens and earth culminates in knowing أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ and that His knowledge encompasses every thing.
terra: In the layered heavens مَّا تَرَىٰ فِى خَلْقِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَٰوُتٍ: created work bears no mismatch, the cosmic form of straight proportion.
terra: Who is the army that could help مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ? The rhetorical question exposes confidence in independent protection as delusion.
terra: Who could provide if God withheld His provision? This reverses the recipient's claim over his share and returns rizq to the One who measures it.
terra: هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَكُمْ وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ attributes both the human and his faculties to one Maker.
terra: The garden owners أَقْسَمُوا۟ لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا turn oath into a plan to cut the crop, concretely joining قسم, human calculation, and presumed control.
terra: وَلَا يَسْتَثْنُونَ shows the garden owners made their sworn harvest plan without reserving it to God's will, clarifying their presumed control.
terra: A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while they sleep, inserting divine power into the calculation they thought complete.
terra: أَن لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا ٱلْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُم مِّسْكِينٌ reveals what their measured plan withholds: the poor person's share.
terra: وَغَدَوْا۟ عَلَىٰ حَرْدٍ قَٰدِرِينَ depicts them setting out convinced of their capacity, the garden-story equivalent of "none can have power over me."
terra: بَلْ نَحْنُ مَحْرُومُونَ reverses their plan: those who meant to deprive the poor discover that their own allotted portion has been withheld.
terra: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ is the final admission that accumulated wealth did not make its possessor self-sufficient.
terra: هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ adds that his authority has vanished too, completing the collapse of imagined wealth and power.
terra: فَمَا مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ عَنْهُ حَٰجِزِينَ says no one could shield even the messenger from divine seizure if he fabricated words, reversing human invulnerability.
terra: تَعَٰلَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا ٱتَّخَذَ صَٰحِبَةً وَلَا وَلَدًا places the exalted Lord outside spouse and offspring.
terra: The jinn conclude أَن لَّن نُّعْجِزَ ٱللَّهَ ... وَلَن نُّعْجِزَهُۥ هَرَبًا: neither earthly position nor flight puts anyone beyond God's power.
terra: قُلْ إِنِّى لَن يُجِيرَنِى مِنَ ٱللَّهِ أَحَدٌ makes the "len ... ahad" construction confess the opposite truth: no one can shelter even the speaker from God.
terra: وَأَحْصَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ عَدَدًۢا states the real counting behind the section's contrast between حساب as enumeration and حسب as supposition.
terra: وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ contrasts God's measuring with humans' inability to count the measure fully.

luna: The section’s dictionary note labels human تقدير as thinking through what to do; this person “فكر وقدر,” making his deliberate calculation a concrete instance of that sense. | terra: إِنَّهُۥ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ is the Qur'an's exact instance of the dictionary sense "the human considers the matter and measures it."

luna: The section connects the person’s own estimate to the root ق د ر; “فقتل كيف قدر” condemns this human measuring, marking its limit beside the Creator’s measure. | terra: فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ condemns the man's self-made estimate, exposing a human use of measure set against the Creator's true measure.
terra: ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ repeats the condemnation and makes the failure of his calculation, rather than mere thought, the passage's emphasis.
terra: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ continues "he thought and measured" with the looking-into-the-matter named in the section's dictionary gloss for human taqdīr.

luna: The section’s “أَيَحْسَبُ” challenges a person’s unsupported estimate; this repeats the question and names his imagined limit—whether God can gather his bones. | terra: أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلْإِنسَانُ أَلَّن نَّجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُۥ repeats the interrogative supposition and makes its object a false limit placed on God's power.

luna: The section calls the eyes, tongue, and lips measured parts; this answer to 75:3 says God can even proportion the fingertips (“نسوي بنانه”), making bodily formation the proof of power. | terra: بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن نُّسَوِّىَ بَنَانَهُۥ answers 75:3 with power to refashion even fingertips, making divine ability an exact bodily proportioning.

luna: The section asks whether a person thinks no one can measure or constrain him; this asks whether he thinks he will be left “سدى,” connecting that presumption to having no governing purpose or limit. | terra: أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلْإِنسَانُ أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى asks whether the human supposes he will be left unmeasured and without a claim upon him.
terra: فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ grounds the rebuke of 75:36 in the human's having been created and proportioned.
terra: فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ continues the crafted-body argument through the making of the two sexes, joining جعل to birth.
terra: أَلَيْسَ ذَٰلِكَ بِقَادِرٍ closes the creation scene by asking whether its Maker has power to restore the dead; created measure is evidence of power.
terra: The human once passed through a span when he was not a thing mentioned, preparing 76:2's claim that his hearing and sight are made rather than self-possessed.

luna: The section calls the eyes, tongue, and lips measured parts; this verse says the created human was made hearing and seeing, tying bodily faculties to human creation. | terra: إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَانَ ... فَجَعَلْنَٰهُ سَمِيعًۢا بَصِيرًا directly joins خلق and جعل in the purposeful making of sensory capacities.
luna: After 76:2’s created, hearing and seeing human, this verse says “إنا هديناه السبيل”; it completes a creation-to-guidance sequence like the one the section sees in 90:4–10.
terra: Silver vessels قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا are proportioned to measure, a material crafting scene that echoes measuring the hide to its intended form.
terra: أَلَمْ نَخْلُقكُّم answers the section's "did We not make" stance by confronting humans with their crafted origin in a lowly fluid.
terra: فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِى قَرَارٍ مَّكِينٍ supplies the bodily scene behind 77:20: the created drop is placed in a secure womb, so جعل is concrete fitting and placement.
terra: إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَّعْلُومٍ gives the womb-stage a known limit, the section's sense of a thing being carried to its appointed boundary.
terra: فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ ٱلْقَادِرُونَ lets the same root name divine determining and divine ability, exactly the double hearing developed in the section.
terra: إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ لَا يَرْجُونَ حِسَابًا identifies refusal to expect an account as the posture behind acting as though no one can measure one's deeds.
terra: وَكُلَّ شَىْءٍ أَحْصَيْنَٰهُ كِتَٰبًا answers 78:27 with a complete written count, opposed to human denial of reckoning.
terra: مِنْ أَىِّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقَهُۥ opens the 80:19 creation-and-measure claim by confronting the human with the material from which he was made.

luna: The section’s root ق د ر includes assigning a measure; “من نطفة خلقه فقدره” says the human was created from a drop and then measured, a close parallel to the measured human form. | terra: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُۥ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ places the human himself under the two acts—created from a drop, then measured—before he can presume autonomy.
terra: ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ follows measured creation with an eased way, paralleling the section's sequence from creating and determining to guiding the two paths.
terra: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُۥ فَأَقْبَرَهُۥ gives the measured human his mortal endpoint, which his self-calculation cannot prevent.
terra: ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُۥ completes the sequence after 80:19 by placing resurrection under the Creator's will and power.

luna: The section imagines a hide measured before it is cut and says the human’s eyes and other parts were measured; this says God created, proportioned, and balanced the person (“فسواك فعدلك”). | terra: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ depicts the human as created, proportioned, and balanced—the body as fitted work.
terra: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ completes 82:7 by describing the bodily form as an intentionally assembled shape.
terra: إِنَّهُۥ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ repeats ظن and لن in a false belief that the prosperous person will never return.
terra: بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ رَبَّهُۥ كَانَ بِهِۦ بَصِيرًا answers 84:14 through the Lord's seeing, joining mistaken immunity to the section's second "does he think no one saw him?"
terra: فَلْيَنظُرِ ٱلْإِنسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ commands the human to examine his own created origin before supposing himself beyond power.
terra: خُلِقَ مِن مَّآءٍ دَافِقٍ answers 86:5 with the lowly material from which the apparently self-sufficient human was crafted.
terra: The fluid's bodily emergence makes 86:6 a concrete generative scene, not an abstract assertion of creation.
terra: إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌ turns the first creation into proof of power to return the human.
terra: يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ adds that concealed things will be exposed, answering the supposition that no one saw.

luna: The section’s root خ ل ق is framed as straight measure; “خلق فسوى” pairs creation with fashioning into due form, making the measured-form image explicit. | terra: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ presents creation as proportioning and setting straight, matching الخلق as "straight measure."

luna: The section follows 90:4 creation with 90:5 power and 90:10 guidance; “قدر فهدى” directly joins measured determination to guidance in that sequence. | terra: وَٱلَّذِى قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ makes measure lead to guidance, the same creation–measure–two-path sequence the section finds across 90:4-10.
terra: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ places the Lord on watch over the powerful peoples just named, preparing the correction of human readings of wealth in 89:15-16.

luna: The section points to 89:16 as one response to measured provision; this preceding ayah supplies the paired ease, which the person reads as honor (“ربي أكرمن”), exposing both judgments as human interpretations. | terra: The tested human treats generous provision as the verdict رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ, supplying the first half of the false human reading whose second half is 89:16.

luna: The section explicitly gives the ق د ر branch “ومن قدر عليه رزقه” as provision narrowed; this verse uses it and quotes the person’s conclusion, “ربي أهانن,” showing how he misreads an allotted measure. | terra: فَقَدَرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقَهُۥ gives the exact "provision was narrowed for him" sense named in the section, while the human wrongly calls the measure humiliation.
terra: كَلَّا بَل لَّا تُكْرِمُونَ ٱلْيَتِيمَ rejects the human verdict about honor and redirects the meaning of provision toward what he does with the vulnerable.
terra: Failure to urge feeding the poor shows that a measured share carries a social claim, completing the correction begun after 89:16.
terra: وَتَأْكُلُونَ ٱلتُّرَاثَ أَكْلًا لَّمًّا depicts inherited portions being swallowed indiscriminately, the corrupt human handling of division.
terra: وَتُحِبُّونَ ٱلْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا names the attachment that makes humans read their allotted wealth as personal rank and power.

luna: The section’s “أحد” is nobody in the man’s boast that no one can overpower him; here “لا يعذب عذابه أحد” turns that negation around, saying no one can punish as the Lord does. | terra: لَّا يُعَذِّبُ عَذَابَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ reverses the boast: on that day "no one" can punish as God punishes.

luna: The section’s negative “أحد” means nobody can reach the man; here “ولا يوثق وثاقه أحد” says nobody binds as the Lord binds, setting an opposite limit on power. | terra: وَلَا يُوثِقُ وَثَاقَهُۥٓ أَحَدٌ completes the reversal with a binding no one can match, the ultimate limit placed on the self-assured man.

luna: The section sees bodily features as measured parts of a created human; this says God created the human “في أحسن تقويم,” adding the image of a form made in due proportion. | terra: لَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَانَ فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ makes the human's creation an excellent setting-straight, close to the section's measured bodily pattern.
terra: خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ establishes the created human origin that makes the later self-sufficient posture in this passage absurd.
terra: كَلَّآ إِنَّ ٱلْإِنسَانَ لَيَطْغَىٰ names the transgression that follows when a created human mistakes his allotted condition for autonomy.
terra: أَن رَّءَاهُ ٱسْتَغْنَىٰ says he transgresses because he sees himself as self-sufficient, the inner premise of "no one has power over me."
terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ gives that self-sufficient human his actual endpoint and owner.

luna: The section’s 90:7 asks whether the man thinks nobody saw him; “ألم يعلم بأن الله يرى” directly reverses that assumption and identifies the unseen observer. | terra: أَلَمْ يَعْلَم بِأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرَىٰ directly answers the human's supposition that no one saw him.
luna: The section’s 90:7 challenges the thought that no one sees the person; this says a person will see even an atom’s weight of good, giving smallest deeds a visible consequence.
luna: Where the section’s man presumes his acts escape notice, this says he will see even an atom’s weight of evil, completing the paired accounting of deeds.
terra: the wealth-hoarder جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ supplies the section's concrete alternative to mere supposition: he counts and recounts the wealth on which he relies.
terra: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ turns that counting into a false supposition that wealth defeats his appointed limit.

luna: The section explains “أحد” in 90:5 as “anyone” under negation; “الله أحد” gives the same named word its divine singular sense, answering the boast’s imagined absence of an overpowering one. | terra: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ lets أَحَد name the One whom the man's negative "no one" leaves out of account.
terra: ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ adds absolute recourse and sufficiency to the One of 112:1, sharpening the contrast with a created man's imagined self-sufficiency.

luna: The section sets 90:3’s parent and offspring against the declaration “لم يلد ولم يولد”; the created line of birth has a boundary in the One who neither begets nor is born. | terra: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ places the One beyond the begetting and being begotten sworn by in 90:3, separating Creator from the created lineage.
terra: وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ is the true absolute negative with أَحَد: no one is His equal, unlike the human's imagined invulnerability.
